issues.description: Class de.tum.in.ase.eist.model.Person: identifier naming mismatch for the first-name property and its accessors. The problem statement and the template/common API use the property name firstName with getFirstName()/setFirstName(); the solution repository's common Person class instead declares the field givenName with getGivenName()/setGivenName(). Other solution code (PersonScene, PersonService) still refer to firstName/getFirstName/setFirstName, causing an internal inconsistency in the solution and a mismatch between the solution's model and the template/problem specification. This will produce compilation failures and prevents building or running the student/client/server code against the solution model as-is.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Person model identifier names consistent across all artifacts. Prefer renaming the solution repository's Person field and accessors from givenName/getGivenName()/setGivenName() to firstName/getFirstName()/setFirstName() so the common model matches the template, problem statement, and the rest of the client/server code. Ensure all references in the solution code compile after the change.

issues.description: The concept is the person's given/first name. The problem statement and the template's Common Person model declare and use the identifier 'firstName' with accessors getFirstName()/setFirstName(). In the solution repository the common Person class declares the field as 'givenName' with getGivenName()/setGivenName(), while other solution code (PersonService and GUI PersonScene) still reference getFirstName()/setFirstName(). This inconsistent identifier for the same concept prevents students from mapping the problem requirements and template to the solution: code that expects getFirstName()/setFirstName() will not compile against a Person class that exposes getGivenName()/setGivenName(), and students will be confused whether to follow 'firstName' or 'givenName'.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the identifier for the person's given name across all artifacts. Preferred: rename the field and accessors in the solution's common Person class from 'givenName' / getGivenName() / setGivenName(...) to 'firstName' / getFirstName() / setFirstName(...) so they match the problem statement and the template. Update any references if necessary. Alternatively, if 'givenName' is preferred, update all template/problem and all service/controller/view code to use 'givenName' consistently. Ensure every usage and import compiles after the change.
